pains.label: We can't run the floor on cold calls any more: RERA fined an office AED 50,000 and suspended nine brokers, and the new telemarketing rules bring fines up to AED 150,000 and cut numbers
pains.definition: The rules against unsolicited calls to owners and residents (RERA/DLD circulars, Cabinet Resolutions 56 and 57 of 2024, TDRA number cuts) and the fines, suspensions and public backlash they bring. Records that report the rule, the fines, or ways residents block and report brokers' calls.

pains.label: The floor lives on 100-125 calls a day per agent to win listings; we need owner numbers, scripts, callers and dialers to keep the volume up
pains.definition: The daily calling grind itself: call quotas, sourcing owner phone numbers and databases, scripts, hiring telesales staff, outsourcing callers, dialers and AI callers. Records where a brokerage hires or buys calling capacity, or an agent describes the grind.

pains.label: Getting enough good leads costs more every year: portal packages and ad rates go up, cost per lead is unpredictable, and many leads are junk or shared
pains.definition: The cost and quality of leads from Property Finder, Bayut, dubizzle, paid ads and lead-gen agencies: rate hikes, cost per lead, leads that do not convert, bought leads that are fake, and brokers building their own portals to escape the big two. Also brokerages hiring lead-generation staff.

pains.label: Leads leak between the portal and the deal: slow follow-up, no attribution, agents hoard or lose leads, so we need a CRM and WhatsApp follow-up to plug it
pains.definition: Losing leads after they arrive: follow-up speed, lead attribution, CRM discipline, agents leaving with leads, automated WhatsApp follow-ups. Records about lead management and CRM tools sold to Dubai brokerages.

pains.label: Agents quit within months: commission-only floors burn people out, hiring is an arms race, retention stays weak
pains.definition: Agent turnover and the constant hiring it forces: commission-only offers, new arrivals who fail, burnout, brokerages advertising agent and team-lead jobs, recruiters selling retention. Records where a brokerage hires agents or someone describes why agents leave.

pains.label: Every ad needs a Trakheesi permit, sold listings must come down within 3 days, max three brokers per listing, and DLD fines AED 50,000 for illegal or fake ads
pains.definition: Advertising and listing rules from DLD/RERA and the portals: Trakheesi permits and their cost, Madmoun QR verification, listing removal deadlines, the three-broker limit, fake-listing crackdowns and the fines that follow.

pains.label: Commission gets dodged, withheld or squeezed: clients skip the fee, sellers cut the middleman, 0% brokers undercut, and brokerages withhold agents' commission
pains.definition: Money owed on a closed deal that does not arrive or is squeezed: unpaid client commission, employers withholding agent commission, buyers avoiding the fee, discount or zero-commission models, VAT absorption.

pains.label: When sales slow, the brokerage feels the squeeze: lay-offs, bankruptcies, and thousands of small agencies may disappear
pains.definition: Market slowdowns and their effect on brokerages: falling transactions, price cuts, lay-offs, bankruptcy, agency shakeouts, brokers taking the model overseas.

pains.label: Licences, RERA cards, exams and visas cost money and time every year for the firm and every agent, and a lapse brings fines
pains.definition: The recurring cost and admin of staying licensed: DET trade licence and its renewal, RERA activity registration, broker cards, DREI course and exam, the annual renewal test, work visas and permits for agents, and the fines for lapses or for working unlicensed.

pains.label: Scams, fake agents and fake listings make clients distrust every broker, so the firm has to prove it is licensed and its ads are real
pains.definition: The trust deficit around Dubai brokers: rental and off-plan scams, unlicensed agents, agents vanishing with deposits, buyers asking whether agents can be trusted, and brokerages publishing scam-avoidance guides to show they are legitimate.
